payload.headline: Netflix at 58.87 stays below fair value; small adds, next at 53.74

summary.thesis: Netflix is a solid, cash-generating business priced below most of its fair-value estimates, but growth is slowing and the price trend is still down.
summary.decision: Long-term: keep adding in small, staggered amounts below the 63.7 DCF base value. Swing: no trade while the price stays under resistance.
summary.act_at: small add below 59.9, next add at 53.74, no buying above 63.7

payload.happening: Netflix closed at 58.87, up 1.33% on the day. It is still in a downtrend, below its 20-day (61.81), 50-day (66.58) and 200-day (79.71) averages, and all three are falling. There is no news since the last note. The next report is on 2027-01-19, and analysts have cut this quarter's EPS estimate (earnings per share) to 0.68 from 0.73.
payload.business: The core business is still healthy. Over the last twelve months revenue was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Operating margin (profit from operations as a share of sales) rose to 31.3% from 29.14%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) grew to 11.4B from 9.0B. The share count fell 3.35% over the year, so each share owns more of the company. What is at risk is the pace of growth. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago. The filings flag a 31% operating margin as the top of its 5-year range of 17–31%, and peaks like that tend to fade. Debt of 12.7B exceeds cash of 8.2B, which leaves a net debt position of 4.4B. That is manageable against 11.4B of yearly free cash flow, but it is not a cushion. The trimmed estimates (next-year EPS revision of -1.1% over 30 days) and the 3 new risk headings in the annual report affect sentiment and disclosure more than demand. The weak tech market and the falling price trend change the mood around the stock, not the business itself.

worth.text: At 58.87 the stock trades at 16.7 times trailing earnings and 15.6 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 4.9, against a peer median of 6.9, and only the 18th percentile of its own 5-year range. The discounted cash flow model (DCF, which values future cash in today's money) gives 37.99 bear, 63.7 base and 76.06 bull. The company's own price-to-sales history gives 58.94 low, 84.5 mid and 122.15 high. The price sits at or below the middle of every method. The current price assumes free cash flow starts growing about 12.2% a year. At 10% starting growth the value is 53.74, and at 20% it is 80.23. The gap between methods comes down to that growth rate and to whether the 31.3% margin holds. If operating margin falls to 23%, the value is 59.9, still just above today's price. If it falls to 15%, the value drops to 39.57. That puts fair value at 53.74 to 80.23, with 63.7 as the anchor.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 10% to 20% a year, close to the 12.2% the price implies, and operating margin does not fall much below 23%.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 11.4B from 9.0B, with a 22.87% free-cash-flow margin.
Price-to-sales of 4.9 is below the 6.9 peer median and at the 18th percentile of its own 5-year history.
The share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each share's claim on profits keeps growing.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
Operating margin of 31.3% is at the top of its 17–31% range; if it falls to 15%, the value is 39.57.
This quarter's EPS estimate was cut 7.3%, to 0.68 from 0.73, ahead of the 2027-01-19 report.

levels.what: Value if operating margin falls to 23%. Small adds below it still have a cushion even if margins fade.
Value at 10% starting cash-flow growth, the low end of the fair-value range. This is the last planned add before the report.
DCF base value. Above it the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: The price of 58.87 is below the DCF base of 63.7, the own-history low of 58.94 and the 59.9 margin-fade value. Estimates are still being trimmed and no support level is listed, so adds stay small and staggered.

swing.why: The trend is down, the price is under every falling average, and resistance sits at 61.14–61.64 and 64.56–65.08. No support level gives a place for a stop, and put open interest is 3.03 times call open interest, so no trade until a close above 65.08.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report falls before the 2027-02-19 option expiry, which prices a move of about 17.1%. So adds stop at the 53.74 slice before the report, and further buying waits for a report that keeps operating margin near 31.3%.

change_mind: If the 2027-01-19 report shows operating margin below 23%, the value falls under 59.9 and the move would be to wait, not add.
If next-year EPS consensus drops below 3.56, today's lowest analyst estimate, the 12.2% implied growth looks too high and adds would pause.
A close above 65.08 would break the resistance ceiling and reopen a swing entry.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still add, confirmed by the 58.87 close holding below the 63.7 DCF base, though today's data moves the margin-fade value to 59.9 and the low add level to 53.74 (from 58.77 and 52.77).
payload.label: Research, not advice.
